http://www.euronews.com/2026/08/10/days-.text: Floods, landslides and accidents driven by a nine-day downpour equivalent to more than a month's worth of rain in some areas have killed at least 13 people in the northern Philippines, rescuers said on Monday.The rains, exacerbated by tropical storms, have led to school and government office closures across the main island of Luzon and flooding in the streets of the capital Manila.Four of the deaths occurred in the mountain resort of Baguio, as a rain-drenched mountainside collapsed on several houses, killing four residents, city disaster official Charles Carame told the AFP news agency.Rescuers were digging through the rubble in search of at least six others who remained missing a day after the incident, he added.State weather forecaster Dan Villamil said rains in the vacation spot four hours north of the capital were already 47% higher than normal for the whole month."The rainfall recorded for August 1-9 was highest in Baguio, with an accumulated 1,413.2 millimetres," he said, adding the city's typical downpour for the month was 963.2 millimetres.Parts of Metro Manila had recorded rain equivalent to about 90% of a typical August, he added.Landslides killed six other people elsewhere on Luzon, while another drowned, one was hit by a falling tree, and one was electrocuted, according to a civil defence office tally.While heavy rain continued to fall early on Monday evening, Public Works Secretary Vince Dizon told a news conference that floodwaters were receding."Our interventions are continuing, but we really need to fix the years and decades' worth of faulty flood mitigation interventions," Dizon told reporters, referencing a scandal over bogus flood-control projects that have cost taxpayers billions of dollars.The Philippines is the first major landmass facing the Pacific cyclone belt and the archipelago is hit by an average of 20 storms and typhoons each year, putting millions of people in disaster-prone areas in a state of constant poverty.Scientists say human-driven climate change is making extreme weather more frequent, prolonged and intense.

https://www.dw.com/en/north-korea-spends.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MOIb On Tuesday, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River, with customs posts and warehousing facilities under construction on both sides of the waterway Image: Yuri Smityuk/TASS/picture alliance Advertisement North Korean leader Kim Jong Un is spending the money that his troops have earned fighting in Ukraine to fund a long wish list of projects that were previously beyond his financial reach. South Korea's National Intelligence Service estimated in May that Pyongyang received a minimum of $7.7 billion (€6.6 billion) in financial aid and economic value from Russia in the preceding three years for committing men and materiel to Moscow's war against Ukraine — and potentially as much as $14 billion. That is a significant amount given that the North's GDP for 2024 stood at $26.6 billion. Kim's support for Russia has been lucrative, and a slew of reports are now identifying where that money is being spent. A portion of the funds is being put aside for the Regional Development 20x10 Policy, unveiled in January 2024 and which aims to construct modern industrial facilities in 20 regional cities per year for the next 10 years to improve living standards outside Pyongyang. Why a new Russia-North Korea road bridge worries Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Benefiting from Russian money More civil programs are being designed, observers say, although most appear to be earmarked for the "elites" who reside in Pyongyang. "Before the alliance with Russia, the general infrastructure was poor due to a mixture of economic mismanagement and sanctions," said Martyn Williams, senior fellow for the Korea program at the Stimson Center in Washington DC. "With the breakdown in consensus on the United Nations Security Council and renewed trade with China and Russia, things are starting to move along now," he told DW. "There are several large programs to build factories and hospitals across the country, [Kim] has ordered the development of entire new districts of Pyongyang and there's a rural housing project building tens of thousands of rural homes," he said, along with investment in "the modernization of several sectors of the economy." There are, however, structural problems that still need to be overcome, he said. "There is investment going into building, but the large new hospital in central Pyongyang was built some time ago and sat unused for a while, until medicines and equipment could be procured," he said. "North Korea is great at building, but keeping it running is the key — so we look to see if that will happen." South Korea proposes talks to officially end war with North To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video IAEA warns of new nuclear facility More of the financial windfall is clearly being put into the military. On Wednesday, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) said it had identified a new uranium enrichment facility at the Yongbyon Nuclear Complex with an estimated 28 cascades of centrifuges. The IAEA estimated that the facility would permit the regime to produce 85 kilograms of weapons-grade highly enriched uranium a year, enough for four nuclear warheads. Satellite images also show that the North is enlarging and upgrading the west coast port of Nampo and Chongjin, on the east coast of the peninsula, to accommodate a new generation of warships. On Monday, Kim attended the commissioning ceremony in Wonsan of the 5,000-ton destroyer Kang Kon, with the North Korean leader claiming the vessel was capable of launching nuclear weapons and would be able to "deal a deadly retaliatory blow at the enemies." The third area of heavy investment has been in major improvements in roads, ports and bridges. This is infrastructure that stagnated during years of isolation under international sanctions but is today required to facilitate the deployment of more troops to Russia and the arrival of advanced military technology, energy and consumer goods in return. On Tuesday, North Korea and Russia opened their first road bridge across the Tumen River, with customs posts and warehousing facilities under construction on both sides of the waterway. The bridge underlines the rapidly expanding ties since Kim and President Vladimir Putin announced a comprehensive strategic partnership in 2024. The route will permit greater truck-borne exchanges, reduce costs and potentially be used for the transit of North Korean men, weapons and ammunition to Russia. It also further reduces the leverage of sanctions on North Korea. North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video "A lot of these projects, such as improving trans-border rail and road connections, building customs facilities and so on, were started before the pandemic and have followed an on-again-off-again pattern ever since," said Marcus Noland, executive vice president at the Peterson Institute for International Economics in Washington. "After difficult times during the pandemic, which was accompanied by border closure, the North Korean economy appears to have grown for the last several years on the back of Ukraine war revenues and cybercrime." Hinterland 'stagnating' Noland said he has the impression that Pyongyang is faring relatively well economically, along with a number of cities on the China border thanks to renewed trade, "but the hinterland continues to stagnate." While the Ukraine conflict and Pyongyang's alliance with Moscow have been an economic boon to North Korea, analysts say, it's not clear what will happen when the war inevitably comes to an end. "The North Korean regime could be in a difficult spot if peace were to break out in Ukraine," said Noland. "If the war-related revenues were to dry up, the country could experience an economic decline and associated discontent after a period of rising expectations," he stressed. "I am not saying that it would be enough to destabilize the system, but I do think that a transition to peace in Ukraine could present challenges that would have to be navigated by the regime." https://www.bgr.com/2256430/ios-27-revie.text: Technology Apps & Software iOS 27 Review: AI Finally Takes Over The iPhone By José Adorno Sept. 11, 2026 4:00 pm EST José Adorno/BGR Add BGR on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover With the Release Candidate version of iOS 27 rolling out just after the iPhone Duo event , we're now just days away from Apple officially releasing iOS 27 to the public on Monday, September 14 . With the foldable iPhone Duo now official and the new iPhone 18 Pro models finally revealed, we now have a clearer picture of the true capabilities of this upcoming software update. Over the past few months, we've been using iOS 27 on an iPhone 17 Pro Max, putting this update to the test all over the world — from mainland China and Paris to Budapest and Berlin. Not only have we noticed significant improvements since the first beta , but also how the new features and changes will reinvigorate Apple's smartphone lineup. While the iPhone 15 Pro and newer models will be acquiring powerful new Siri AI features, Apple says that older models will get snappier with tons of bug fixes, improved AirDrop reliability, and apps opening faster than ever. After months of testing, we've learned about how the new features improve the iPhone experience, how the update impacts battery life, and who should be updating to this software once it becomes available for the iPhone 11 and beyond. Here's everything you need to know about iOS 27, Apple's biggest leap into AI so far. Liquid Glass has reached its final form José Adorno/BGR Visually, iOS 27 looks similar to iOS 26, but it's far more polished. Some apps have improved contrast and look more vivid. Even the Clear option for Liquid Glass, which on iOS 26 was washed out and hard to see with some backgrounds, has evolved. The entire iOS 26 update cycle seemed to focus on fixes and changes for Liquid Glass, but it took until the arrival of iOS 27 to bring the new design language up to the company's typical standards. Liquid Glass has been Apple's push into a more unified design language across its operating systems, and, unlike during the Steve Jobs era, the company is willing to make compromises to appease users. For example, users can decide whether they want a glassy, translucent experience or a tinted look closer to iOS 18. In general, refraction is more uniform across the OS with the latest update. It's also important to note that the company requires iOS 27 apps to be easily resized to any format of display, which we now know was an effort to maximize compatibility with the foldable iPhone Duo. iOS 27 not only looks beautiful, but owners of older iPhones should notice apps opening faster. With the modern powerhouse that is the iPhone 17 Pro Max, it's impossible to say that Instagram, iMessage, and other apps were suddenly opening dramatically faster, as the experience remains consistent with what was already present in iOS 26. Siri AI is incredibly useful José Adorno/BGR Apple's long-delayed promise of Apple Intelligence is finally a reality — even if it's still in beta. Rolling out to users globally in iOS 27 – except for those with a European Apple Account – the new Siri AI seems to be everything the company envisioned and, perhaps, a little bit more. It's such an enormous leap forward from Siri having a hard time setting a timer, sharing a weather report, or knowing what month it is . The truth is, Siri AI is incredibly useful, and it's yet another push for the company's own services. The personal assistant shines when it's accessing Messages, Notes, Mail, and other first-party Apple apps. Nine out of 10 times, Siri was able to help me find a very specific message, document, podcast link, or even something I didn't fully remember. The personal assistant is conversational, gives me insights about my travel, can answer nearly any question, and translates on the fly. I've ever used it to figure out exactly how early I should wake up to eat breakfast before leaving a hotel for the airport. Of course, Siri is not always perfect, and it sometimes forgets it can use Google. For example, if I ask for translation of an unsupported language like Hungarian, the personal assistant quickly tells me it's incapable of doing that. However, all it takes is reminding Siri it can browse the internet to find the translation online. Other features that have impressed me include asking Siri to replace a phrase with translated copy, adding information to a form, and proactively making my day easier by rearranging my schedule to avoid conflicts. Apple Intelligence has reached a new level José Adorno/BGR Every Apple Intelligence feature has been upgraded. Genmoji creation, for example is very proactive as you send messages — even though Apple will suggest some bizarre images. Image generation is also faster on Image Playground, Writing Tools is a constant reminder you might not know how to construct a phrase properly, and the AI-powered image editing tools impressed me the same way Pixelmator did years ago with how it used the iPad's machine learning capabilities to remove objects from photos. iOS 27 features an improved Clean Up tool, which is much better at removing unwanted objects and people in the background of your photos. The Expand tool is great for adding to your photo to fill out the frame, and it also works surprisingly well. Finally, the ability to use Spatial Reframing, which lets you tweak the angle of a photo, almost makes me question if we should have so much added control over our shots. While there's plenty worth being excited about, and anyone with an iPhone 15 Pro or newer model is going to have a wealth of new features to explore — after they join the wait list for the new AI features, anyway – it's also somewhat odd to be celebrating the efforts of a trillion-dollar company that is only now catching up with the demand for AI. Even though I'd consider Apple Intelligence one of the best applications of AI on the market, Apple took its sweet time getting here. That said, there's no shame in asking Google for help — I just wish Apple had done so sooner. General improvements and battery life José Adorno/BGR Besides the full adoption of AI, iOS 27 is fundamentally a minor upgrade. There are no notable new features for Apple Music, most of Apple's apps look the same, and highly-anticipated additions, like the ability to update passwords with a single tap, aren't ready yet. Rather, Apple decided to deliver an update focused on fixing bugs, polishing up the code, and making the experience feel snappier. For an iPhone 17 Pro Max user, it's honestly hard to tell the difference between iOS 26 and iOS 27. After all, every beta release introduces new bugs, though, with the iOS 27 Release Candidate now installed on my device, I can say that the software feels as stable as ever. For owners of an iPhone 12 or an iPhone 13, their devices should feel even faster than they did on iOS 26. Of course, battery life is always a major concern when updates arrive. I've been charging my iPhone twice a day throughout the summer, which is due to a mix of Parisian heatwaves, testing every Siri AI feature, and a seemingly dry vapor chamber (that's not really how it works, but my iPhone 17 Pro Max does feel warmer around the camera plateau). However, for those who haven't been using the iOS 27 beta, Apple has been doing something clever: indexing Siri and its apps for the iOS 27 release . What this means is that, the iOS 26.6 update already did most of the hard work, so iOS 27 should run even better than usual on day one. For me, every weekly update means a new round of indexing. Should you upgrade to iOS 27? José Adorno/BGR iOS 27 is a welcome upgrade for any iPhone owner — even those without the latest models and those who aren't interested in upgrading to an iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo. While an iPhone 11 owner might not find many new features in iOS 27, they will gain a more reliable AirDrop, faster speeds, and some battery improvements. For those with an iPhone 15 Pro or newer, the highlight is Apple Intelligence, which truly transforms the iPhone experience. I personally really enjoy how the new Siri lives on the Dynamic Island and how notifications sit right next to the clock. That said, iPhone users will need to retrain their brains a bit, as the upper-right corner is dedicated to the Control Center, the upper-left corner is for notifications, and everything else around the top of the display is Siri AI and Spotlight. Overall, I've been satisfied with iOS 27, and I'm looking forward to see what the new cycle of updates will bring. iOS 27.1 is still a mystery for now — it could add even more AI features or just make small tweaks. We've also put together a checklist to prepare your iPhone for iOS 27 , which is worth reading before the launch on September 14. Overall, this is one of the most polished software updates Apple has delivered in recent years. Recommended

https://telex.hu/belfold/2026/10/22/kleb.text: Menü Kereső Közleményben reagált a Klebelsberg Központ a civil szervezet iskolai foglalkozására, amire rászállt a fideszes propaganda Belföld Aradi Hanga Zsófia Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! Beállítom A Klebelsberg Központ amint értesült az Újpetrei Általános Iskolában a közelmúltban megtartott foglalkozásról, haladéktalanul felvette az iskolát fenntartó Mohácsi Tankerületi Központtal a kapcsolatot, és részletes tájékoztatást kért a kialakult helyzet tisztázása érdekében – írta a Klebelsberg Központ (KK) csütörtökön a Telexhez eljuttatott közleményében. Pont egy hete számoltunk be arról , hogy a komplett (megmaradt) fideszes propagandagépezet, a Fidesz, a KDNP és a Mi Hazánk politikusai is rászálltak a Pécsi Emberség Erejével Alapítványra (EEA), miután a szervezet a Facebook-oldalán számolt be egy foglalkozásról, amit az újpetrei iskolában tartottak. A politikusok és influenszerek is arra utalgattak bejegyzéseikben, hogy a szervezet egy nappal a „tiszás törvény” elfogadása után LMTQ-érzékenyítést tartott a gyerekeknek. Ez a valóságtól nagyon távol áll, a Telex megkeresésére az EEA részletesen elmagyarázta, hogy pályaorientációs foglalkozást tartottak az iskolában, ahol társasjáték segítségével arról beszélgettek a munkatársaik a gyerekekkel, hogy vannak foglalkozások, hobbik és tárgyak is, amiket a többségi társadalom lányosnak vagy fiúsnak tart, azonban teljesen rendben van, ha valaki lány létére például informatikus szeretne lenni, vagy fiúként szeret táncolni. A szervezet vezetője hangsúlyozta, a rendezvény minden hatályos törvénynek megfelelt, és végig pedagógus jelenlétével zajlott. A foglalkozás körüli felháborodásra az iskola igazgatója is reagált, azt írta, az egyik osztályfőnök kezdeményezésére valósult meg a foglalkozás, amihez mint intézményvezető hozzá is járult. Azt is hangsúlyozta, hogy semmilyen szexuális, nemi élettel vagy orientációval kapcsolatos téma nem merült fel az eseményen. A KK bő egy héttel azután, hogy a jobboldali propaganda rászállt a foglalkozásra kiadott egy közleményt, amelyben azt írta, „elvárja az intézményektől a jogszerű működést, különös tekintettel a gyerekeknek megtartott foglalkozásokkal kapcsolatban. A gyermekközpontú oktatás alapja a gyermekek biztonsága, jólléte és egészséges fejlődése. A gyermekek érdeke mindenek felett áll.” A KK szerint az elmúlt napokban pont az ő érdekük sérült, ezért arra kérnek mindennkit, hogy „az Újpetrei Általános Iskola mindennapi életét, az ott tanuló gyerekek nyugalmát, tanulását ne zavarják! Külön megkérjük a médiumok képviselőit, hogy az iskolába menet a gyermekeket ne zaklassák, róluk felvételeket ne készítsenek! Legyenek partnereink, hogy a napi politikai csatározásoktól megkíméljük őket!” Az EEA egyébként már múlt héten törölte a bejegyzéséből a foglalkozásról készült képeket, miután azok terjedni kezdtek a fideszes influenszerek posztjain keresztül. A szervezet vezetője ezt azzal indokolta, „nagyon problémás, hogy valótlan tartalmú bejegyzésekben terjednek a gyerekekről készült fotók”. A Tisza korábban már megígérte , hogy az oktatási rendszert lépésről lépésre fogja átalakítani, ennek részeként az iskolavezetők visszakapják a munkáltatói jogokat, ismét ők dönthetnek majd a tanárok kinevezéséről, a Klebelsberg Központ pedig ugyan nem szűnik meg, de oktatástámogatási háttérintézményként működik majd tovább.
